title: Transmit application catalog
description: What Transmit knows about an application: where it keeps its state, what is inside that, and what has to happen to each part when it moves to another system. A user can drop a file in this shape into the configuration directory to describe an application Transmit has never heard of.

schemaVersion.description: 2 for this shape. Version 1 wrote one path per system directly on each state root and had no contents or move rules; it is still read, for ever, so an overlay written against it keeps working.

tokenisedPath.description: A path starting with a known-folder token, such as {HOME}/.config/app. Anything else resolves to nothing and the application then looks as though it has no state at all.

id.description: Reverse-DNS, stable across versions and systems. A second recipe with the same id replaces the first, which is how an overlay corrects a built-in entry.

detect.description: What each system's package manager or application registry calls it.

install.description: Package names per package manager, for the script the restore writes. Transmit never runs that script itself.

quiesce.description: Processes to ask the user to close, so the state is captured whole rather than half way through a write.

id.description: Unique within the recipe, so a move step can say which root it means.

paths.description: Candidates per system, in order of preference: the first that exists is used. A list rather than one path is what lets a Flatpak or Snap install be found beside a native one.

content.description: One thing inside a state folder. Naming what it is decides what happens to it: an index has to be rewritten, a cache is never worth carrying, a credential must not travel unless the archive is encrypted and the user asked for it.

portable.description: always: copies and works. rewrite: works once the paths inside it are corrected. same-os: only meaningful on the same system. never: regenerable or machine-specific.

live.description: May be open and being written while the capture runs, so it is read through the consistent-copy path rather than straight off disk.

moveStep.description: This file, moving from here to there, is handled like this.

set.description: For rewrite: settings to force to a fixed value, which is a different job from correcting a path.

rewriteRule.description: A file whose contents name locations on the old machine, and exactly where those names are. Deliberately narrow: a blanket search and replace across restored files would eventually corrupt something.

carries_data.description: Whether this application's own data can travel at all. False means Transmit can record that it was installed and nothing more.

pairs.description: How well it survives one particular journey. The most specific entry wins, so a recipe can say 'adapted everywhere, except to Windows' without repeating itself.
